newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply higher on good volume.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply higher on good volume.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended sharply higher Wednesday, on good volume, as this week's shortcovering rally gathered pace after the LME February options declaration, traders said.
"It was a combination of factors, but the market is now looking very bullish," Dean Witter trader Mike Frawley, said.
"The market was expecting some weakness after the LME February options declaration but the spreads tightened and the COMEX March contract pushed up through January's highs," he said.
COMEX March copper ended up 4.75 cents at 108.75 cents a pound, after posting a new six month high for the contract at 108.80. Total estimated volume for COMEX copper futures was a high 15,000 lots.
The LME cash-to-three month spread widened early Wednesday to around $180 a tonne, before closing around $150, after easing to around $111.00 a tonne Tuesday.
The COMEX March/May spread ended at 3.70 cents a pound Wednesday, up from 2.70 cents Tuesday, but down from the January highs near 4.0 cents a pound.

In the past three months copper prices have been recovering steadily from two-year lows seen in mid-1996, when, after the Sumitomo scandal, prices fell to levels that restricted the supply of scrap onto the prompt market.
"We strongly suspect the Chinese will return to the market as buyers in late February or early March," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.
"This buying interest will coincide with some Japanese buying for GSP (preferential tariff purchases) and a seasonal pick up in construction activity," he said.
"So whatever happens, do not short the market as a big backwardation could reappear in the next few months," he said.
